title: AleFire-Library FB FSM definition
description: One file per controlling FB (not per UDT/device page). Captures states, transitions, guards, timers, entry actions and free-text notes for a single finite state machine, sourced from the FB's .s7dcl. Devices with a single FSM get one file; load-cells' Loading/Unloading FBs each get their own sibling file in the same device doc directory. Free text is English regardless of docs locale — IT/EN prose is generated from it, not stored per-locale.

schema_version.description: Schema version this file conforms to, e.g. "1.0". Bump on structural changes.

fb.description: Controlling FB name, e.g. "SS_valve". Matches dist/library_manifest.json fbs.<UDT>.ctrl.name.

udt.description: UDT this FB operates on via its VAR_IN_OUT param. Matches a dist/library_manifest.json udts key.

source.description: Path to the FB's .s7dcl, relative to raw/, for traceability back to the SCL this was derived from.

delegates.description: Present only when this FB hands its whole FSM or just its timer off to an embedded child instance (e.g. Sigillata SS delegates its FSM to XV; Deviatore delegates actuator_timeout to XVA/XVB). Omit entirely when the FB owns both.

fsm.description: Tag of the child instance the whole FSM delegates to (e.g. "XV"). When set, this file has no states/transitions/timers of its own — the doc generator omits Diagramma di stato and Timer entirely and cross-references the named child instead.

timer.description: Tag(s) of the child instance(s) the timer delegates to (e.g. ["XVA", "XVB"]). When set (and fsm is not), the doc generator omits only the Timer section.

label.description: Mermaid composite-state label wrapping the whole diagram, ALL CAPS by convention (e.g. "SS_VALVE", "LOADING_FB").

states.description: Top-level state tree. Nesting mirrors mermaid's `state X { ... }` composite states. Not every FB nests two levels deep — flat FBs (e.g. Unloading, Solenoid_valve) just have one level.

transitions.description: Flat list of edges. "from" may be the literal "[*]" (initial pseudostate); "to"/"from" state references use dot-separated paths for nested states (e.g. "NORMAL.CLOSED").

guard_formulas.description: Named composite guards (e.g. internal_error := A OR B OR ...). Rendered as the standalone ```Pascal code block that adjoins the diagram. Omit when the FB has no such named composite guard (e.g. load-cells inlines plain-language guards directly on transitions instead).

timers.description: Omit (or leave empty) when this FB has no TON_TIME of its own — either it has none at all (e.g. Solenoid_valve, immediate transition) or it delegates timing to a child (see delegates.timer).

entry_actions.description: Omit (or leave empty) when this FB has no REGION Entry actions — most FBs don't; today only Loading/Unloading do.

notes.description: Free-text FB-level "why" notes worth surfacing in the Funzionamento prose (e.g. a timer ORing two sibling states, an asymmetric FAULT-recovery path, an acknowledged bug comment in the source). English, one note per list item.

id.description: Symbolic state name, matching the FB's own VAR CONSTANT name (e.g. "CLOSED", "OPENING"). Never a raw numeric value — per-file integer values aren't meaningful across FBs.

description.description: Short English description of what this state means physically. Optional — omit for states that are self-explanatory (e.g. pure routing intermediates).

outputs.description: Map of physical output device tag -> value while in this state (e.g. {"XY": true}). Only meaningful for states with a fixed, deterministic output; omit for states where output isn't a simple constant.

children.description: Nested substates, only present for composite states (e.g. NORMAL containing CLOSED/OPENING/OPEN/CLOSING).

from.description: Source state path (dot-separated for nested states), or the literal "[*]" for an initial pseudostate edge.

to.description: Destination state path (dot-separated for nested states).

guard.description: Guard condition as boolean-expression-like text (e.g. "ZSL & !ZSH") or, for edges with no single boolean (e.g. an ambiguous-first-scan case), a short plain-language condition. Omit for unconditional transitions.

note.description: Optional free-text explaining a non-obvious transition, e.g. FAULT recovery re-deriving the destination from live sensors rather than returning to a fixed prior state.

name.description: Symbolic name of the composite guard, as declared/computed in the FB (e.g. "internal_error").

expression.description: The boolean expression exactly as it reads in source (e.g. "sensor_mismatch OR sensor_conflict OR failed_to_close OR failed_to_open").

active_states.description: State path(s) the timer's IN condition evaluates true for. A list because IN frequently ORs multiple sibling states together (e.g. active during both OPENING and CLOSING) — never assume single-state activity from the timer's name.

param.description: Dotted path to the SETTING field bound to the timer's PT (e.g. "SETTING.actuator_timeout").

raises.description: Optional free text describing what the timer's .Q output drives (e.g. an ALARMS field it sets, or a guard it feeds into).

state.description: State path this one-shot entry action fires for (e.g. "NORMAL.IDLE").

shadow_var.description: Name of the prev_state/prev_normal_state shadow variable gating this action, for traceability back to source (e.g. "prev_normal_state").

actions.description: Free-text description of each one-shot write fired on entering this state (e.g. "BATCH.transferred := 0", "STATUS.LOADING.loading_finished pulses 1 scan TRUE").
